diet.text: Varies by area - slugs, fish, frogs and more

overview.text: The Western Terrestrial Garter Snake is a medium-sized garter snake of western North America. It is so variable in colour that even experts find it hard to identify.

identification.text: Usually a yellow, light orange or white stripe down the back and a paler stripe on each side; some have red or black spots between the stripes.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Western North America: central British Columbia, Alberta and south-western Manitoba in Canada, the western United States east to western Nebraska, and an isolated population in Baja California, Mexico.

habitat.text: Grasslands, woodlands and conifer forests from sea level up to about 3,960 m. Mostly a land snake, but some mountain populations live partly in water.

diet.text: Eats whatever is common where it lives, so its diet changes from place to place - coastal and inland snakes eat quite different prey.

reproduction.text: Gives birth to 8 to 12 live young in August and September.
